TC.description:
Cycle-length selector. Two timing bits combined into a single
4-value field:
  00 = FAST
  01 = NORM
  10 = SLOW
  11 = WAIT

0.name: FAST
0.description: Fast microcycle, approx. 150 ns. Only available on ND-100 with the 'fast option' hardware. Not used on standard ND-100.

1.name: INTERMEDIATE
1.description: Intermediate microcycle, approx. 170 ns. Not used on standard ND-100; manual lists the value for completeness.

2.name: SLOW
2.description: Slow microcycle, approx. 190 ns. Default on standard ND-100.

3.name: WAIT
3.description: Wait for bus-control synchronization (variable; used to synchronise with memory / bus handshakes).

TC.notes:
Per the manual: "In NORD-100 all microinstructions are either
'slow' or 'wait'." FAST and INTERMEDIATE are not used on the
standard ND-100. The "fast option" variant replaces most SLOW
microinstructions with FAST while retaining WAIT where needed.

Microinstructions that MUST stay SLOW even on a fast-option
ND-100 (component timing constraint):
  1. All UART microinstructions (SIOC, RSDA, TBSTR).
  2. Microinstructions whose IDB-source result is used by the
     ALU as an arithmetic operand and then tested with F=0 in
     the next microinstruction.
  3. All microinstructions touching the memory management
     module (IDBS,MMR or COMM,LDIR or COMM,XMMI).

On ND-100 there is no equivalent of ND-110's BIT20 branch-
address extension. The microcode branch address field is 12
bits wide (CSBIT_11_0), with branch-source selection instead
controlled by the VECT0 / SLWCS0 / MAPJ0 / MIS decoder at
bits 25-27 + 42-43.

VECT0.description:
Inverted VECT. When 0 (active), the lower 4 bits of the branch
target are taken from one of IR / ALD / RA (selected by MIS)
instead of from PROM bits 0:3. When 1 (inactive), PROM supplies
all 12 bits of the branch target.
VECT0.notes: On ND-110 this bit is called simply VECT (not inverted), and works differently - see nd110-fields.yaml.

SLWCS0.description:
Inverted slow-CS / WCS-load enable. When 0 (active), initiates
START LOAD WRITABLE CS regardless of VECT0/MAPJ0 - the current
microinstruction loads the writable control store instead of
branching normally.
SLWCS0.notes: On ND-110 bit 26 is DLY0 (microcycle delay control).

MAPJ0.description:
Inverted map-jump enable. When 0 (active) with SLWCS0=1 and
VECT0=1, dispatches to the macro-opcode decode-PLA address for
the current macroinstruction (or to the interrupt vector
entry if /INT RQ is asserted).
MAPJ0.notes: On ND-110 bit 27 is DLY1 (microcycle delay control).

IDBS.notes:
The ND-110 extended this field to 5 bits (repurposing what was
bit 41 = SEXT on ND-100) and added extra IDBS sources in the
upper range 0o20..0o37. ND-100 IDBS codes occupy only the
range 0o00..0o17.

SEXT.description:
Sign-Extend modifier for the IDBS source. When set (together
with IDBS = GPR, which is the primary documented use case),
the GPR value is sign-extended from bit 7 to bits 8-15 as it
is latched onto the IDB. This eases address-calculation and
argument-instruction code paths.
SEXT.reference: ND-06.018.01 p.20 line 524 (IDBS entry '22 octal' = GPR with sign extension)
SEXT.notes:
The ND-110 reuses this bit as the top bit of IDBS, expanding
the source count from 16 to 32. ND-100 keeps IDBS at 16 sources
and uses bit 41 for this sign-extend modifier. In the manual's
IDBS table the composite "22 octal" row appears between the
standard 0..17 entries - it represents IDBS=2 (GPR) combined
with bit 41 set, producing the sign-extended GPR source. The
ND-110 retains an equivalent compound token (IDBS,GPR,SEXT)
even though it encodes it into a dedicated 5-bit IDBS code
rather than a separate modifier bit.

MIS.description:
Two-bit multi-role field. All three roles are confirmed on
ND-100:
  (a) Shift mode when ALUM = 11 (shift instruction):
        00 = ASH  (arithmetic shift)
        01 = ROT  (rotational shift)
        10 = ZIN  (zero-end-input shift)
        11 = LIR  (link-end-input shift)
  (b) Page mode on memory-op COMMs
      (EXRQ/IRDRQ/DERQ/RDRQ/WRRQ):
        00 = fetch / physical address (no paging)
        01 = PT    (normal page table)
        10 = APT   (alternative page table)
        11 = HOLD  (last-used page table)
  (c) Lower-4-bits source for vectored jumps (VECT0=0):
        00 = IR(0..3)    (used by TRA, TRR)
        01 = IR(8..10)   (used in memory-reference addr calc)
        10 = ALD(0..3)
        11 = A-operand bits
All three roles share the same two bits; the active role is
determined by the other fields (ALUM, COMM, VECT0) of the
same microinstruction.

CSBIT_11_0.description: Branch address (when SCOND=0). The effective 13-bit branch address is (CSBIT20 << 12) | CSBIT_11_0.

TSEL.description: Test Selector - selects which condition to test (only when SCOND=1)

F_SEQ.description: False-path sequence control (F,JMP / F,NEXT / F,RETURN). Only when SCOND=1.

F_STK.description: False-path stack operation (F,HOLD / F,POP / F,LOAD / F,PUSH). Only when SCOND=1.

CSBIT20.description: Address Extension Bit - high bit (bit 12) of the 13-bit branch address

CSDELAY_BIT21.description: Delay control bit (timing-related; ignored for logical comparisons)
CSDELAY_BIT21.notes: Part of the delay/timing control, see microcode.h and ND110MicroCode/Program.cs

LOOP.description: LCOUNT - Count loop counter; if result false, return and hold

CONDENABL.description: Enable conditional sequencing. When set, use FALSE-path specs if condition is false.

SCOND.description: Set Condition - when set, the lower 12 bits encode condition tests (LCC/TSEL/F_SEQ/F_STK) instead of a branch address.

CSDELAY_BITS_27_26.description: Delay control bits (timing-related; ignored for logical comparisons)

T_STK.description: True-path stack operation (T,HOLD / T,POP / T,LOAD / T,PUSH)

T_SEQ.description: True-path sequence control (T,JMP / T,RETURN / T,NEXT / T,JMP0-3)

COMM.description: Command field - selects a 5-bit command code

IDBS.description: Internal Data Bus Source - selects what drives the IDB

MIS.description: MISO field - shift mode when ALUM=MIC (ROT/ZIN/LIN)

ALUSRC_STS.description: ALU Mode Control / Status update (STS,LO / STS,EA / STS,ES)

ALUI.description:
ALU Function Select. This 9-bit field encodes the composite ALU operation
(source operand selector + function + carry-in combination). It is decoded
as a single ALUF,xxx token (see tokens/nd110-tokens.yaml for all ALUF,xxx
entries and their w4 encodings).
ALUI.notes:
For ND-110, only bits 55-63 of the 64-bit canonical form map here.
In the 48-bit ND-110 word, this field occupies the upper 9 bits.

line_2.name: Bus and Sequencing

line_3.description: Branch target OR condition test and false-path sequencing

rom_bit_flip.description: ND-120 EPROM images have bits 22-27 inverted vs the assembled form
rom_bit_flip.purpose:
When reading raw EPROM contents (e.g. from 45132L.bin + 45133L.bin),
XOR with this mask to obtain the canonical assembled form used by the
assembler and disassembler. When writing ROMs, apply the same XOR in
reverse.
